I farm this small sorghum plot here in Benshagul Gumuz, only a bit more than a quarter of my land. The rains here are usually enough for sorghum, so I do not worry too much about water, but fertilizer costs money I do not always have. I went to school a little, so I know DAP helps, but for sorghum most of us here just use what manure we have from the goats and chickens — the cooperative fertilizer usually goes to the maize plot first. I keep my own sorghum seed from last harvest like my father did, and I intercrop with some beans and a little pumpkin to get more from the small piece of land.

I will not buy chemical fertilizer for this plot this season — the plot is too small (0.12 ha), one bag of DAP is too much and too expensive just for this, and I would rather save the cash for the maize. I will spread the little manure I have from the animals. I use my saved local sorghum seed, no pesticide because pests have not been bad, no irrigation because I depend on the rains. Most of the work is me and my wife; at weeding time I may call on a neighbor or two for a couple of days through labor-sharing, but I do not really pay cash for hired workers on such a small plot.
